question: Consider $A = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & a \\ -a & 0 \end{pmatrix}$ and $B = \begin{pmatrix} b & 0 \\ 0 & d \end{pmatrix}$. For which values of $a, b, d$ is $AB$ symmetric for all $a \neq 0$?
explanation:
Calculate $AB$:

$AB = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & a \\ -a & 0 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} b & 0 \\ 0 & d \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \times b + a \times 0 & 0 \times 0 + a \times d \\ -a \times b + 0 \times 0 & -a \times 0 + 0 \times d \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & ad \\ -ab & 0 \end{pmatrix}$

This is symmetric only if $ad = -ab$, i.e., $d = -b$, so (b) is correct.

Correct Option: (b)

options.D: $a$ can be any value, $b, d$ arbitrary
